title: How to Invest for an AI Boom, AI Bust, or...Both: These ETFs Can Help.
author: Ben Gran
description: With uncertainty surrounding whether the AI boom will deliver returns or become another bubble, investors face three scenarios: betting on AI winners through tech-heavy ETFs, hedging against an AI bust with bonds and international stocks, or diversifying across mid-cap and small-cap stocks to capture broader economic gains. The article recommends different ETF strategies based on individual beliefs about AI's future profitability.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended for investors bullish on AI boom; tech-heavy portfolio (65.8% tech) with strong 5-year average annual returns of 14.3%, providing concentrated exposure to major AI beneficiaries.
Positioned as a balanced AI boom play with more diversification than Nasdaq-100 (44.3% tech); solid 5-year returns of 13.2% with lower expense ratio of 0.04%.
Recommended for adventurous AI boom believers; provides full AI value chain exposure across infrastructure, services, and software with 49 focused holdings.
Recommended as hedge against AI bust scenario; bonds typically appreciate when stocks decline, offering portfolio protection during market downturns.
Suggested for AI bust protection; diversifies away from U.S. tech concentration with 3,852 global stocks, offering alternative growth if U.S. market slumps.
Recommended for balanced AI boom/bust scenario; only 14.4% tech exposure provides diversification beyond major tech names with 31-year track record of 11.3% average returns.
Suggested for investors believing AI gains will be widely distributed; small-cap exposure (1,997 stocks) captures potential winners outside major tech companies.

title: The S&P 500 Just Did Something Seen Only 1 Other Time Since 1871 — and It's Not Good News for Wall Street
author: Keith Speights
description: The S&P 500 Shiller CAPE ratio has reached 40 for only the second time in 155 years (first in 1999, now in June 2026). Historically, such elevated valuations have preceded major market downturns, including the dot-com bubble crash and the Great Depression. While current earnings are rising faster than valuations unlike in 1999, investors should focus on high-quality stocks with reasonable valuations and consider building cash reserves for potential market sell-offs.

title: 3 Magnificent ETFs I'm Buying Hand Over Fist in 2026
author: Stefon Walters
description: The author recommends three complementary ETFs for 2026: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) for broad U.S. market exposure, Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) for income from high-quality dividend stocks, and Invesco Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQM) for growth exposure to large-cap tech companies. Together, they provide diversification across growth, income, and stability.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as a foundational portfolio holding with proven long-term wealth-building track record. Author notes respectable 9.3% YTD returns and positions it for fourth consecutive year of double-digit gains.

Highlighted as consistent market outperformer with 15.8% average annual returns since inception. Provides growth exposure to large-cap companies, though noted as tech-heavy with 65.75% sector concentration.

title: This ETF Is Down 7% From Its High. History Says Now Is a Smart Time to Invest.
author: Stefon Walters
description: The Invesco Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQM) has declined 7% from its June high but remains up 12.7% year-to-date.
